criteria.evidence: Every guided section is present and substantive: What it does (three bullets: when it runs, what the questions cover, what it produces), Inputs / Outputs (three ins, two outs with their shape: "each question with its id, its plain question, its choices and its proposed answer with the source of that answer"), Rules & behavior (eight rules incl. tier-missing, out-of-choice correction, partial reply), seven Given/When/Then criteria, Out of scope naming four owners, and an Agent intent (ICE) with Goal, Limit, Fails if, Context and Checked by.

"A choice is offered only when Phoenix memory holds it. A domain, standard or tool that memory does not hold is never a choice, because initialize could not set up memory for it."; "The questions are asked together in one brief, not one at a time, so the person sees the whole set-up at once."; "No unanswered question is recorded as an answer, and no proposal stands in for it, because an answer the person did not give is not the person's."

Discrete bullets throughout; the feature states the function's behavior ("Runs when the product owner starts `initialize` after the install. It reads Phoenix memory through the memory tool and builds one short set of questions"), never a user story; acceptance is Given/When/Then: "Given a reply that answers four of six questions, when initialize reads it, then it asks again only for the two unanswered questions, keeps the four answers, and records no answer for the two until the person gives one."

The parent capability states only "Each question has choices and a proposed answer with its source" and lists the feature in one line; the feature adds the input sources of choices and proposals, the output shape, and branches the parent never covers: "When the memory tool cannot reach Phoenix memory (it says a tier is missing), initialize says so in plain words and stops", the correction outside the choices, and the partial reply.

What: "builds one short set of questions about the project from what memory holds"; why: "These are the facts that decide which memory and which review rules fit." and "The confirmed answers are the input of every other feature of initialize."; edges: "Building the project's memory from the answers (fn-project-memory owns it)." A cold reader learns what Phoenix memory holds from the Inputs line ("the domain shelves, the technology standards, the tools and frameworks it holds, and the review rule groups").
